title: Plates from a Collection
subtitle: How a folder of pictures becomes a matched set of plates, and the plates become a book.
author: Renaise Kim
prompt: Four objects from a museum's open collection, each one photographed as a specimen on black. Make them into a short manual: what the objects are, how to ask a model for a plate, and how to keep a set of plates looking like one book.

cover.label: Cover
cover.caption: Plate 00 from plate-book.json (run 2, seed 20261103), mapped by brightness to the seven tones at right. AI-generated.

about.head: Collection
about.body: Four museum photographs, all public domain (CC0) from The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access: a faience hippopotamus, a netsuke, a watch and a toy. The first three went into the workflow.

about.head: Plates
about.body: Five plates from one run of plate-book.json on Comfy Cloud (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, an open-weight model, Lightning 4-step, seed 20261103): a cover, one plate per object and a group plate. Every generated picture is marked AI-generated in its caption.

about.head: Layout
about.body: Set by make_book.py from this prompt, the folder of images and a spec file. Same inputs, same book.

chapters.title: Four objects from one museum
chapters.dek: The collection this book starts from.

notes.head: Public domain only
notes.body: Every object here is released CC0 by The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Check the licence before a photo goes into the folder.

notes.head: One object per photo
notes.body: A single thing on a plain ground. The model keeps whatever else is in the frame, labels and rulers included.

notes.head: Keep the museum's light
notes.body: Collection photos already show shape and material clearly. Do not re-light or retouch them first.

notes.head: Write down what it is
notes.body: Name, place, date, accession number. The caption is also the first line of the prompt.

images.caption: Hippopotamus (“William”), Egypt, ca. 1961–1878 B.C. Met 17.9.1. CC0.

images.label: Object 3
images.caption: Watch, ca. 1630–40, Johann Possdorfer. Met 17.190.1525. CC0.

chapters.title: Read the object before you prompt
chapters.dek: What to look at first, so you can ask for it by name.

notes.head: Shape
notes.body: Seated, coiled, round, flat. One word for the silhouette keeps it from drifting.

notes.head: Material
notes.body: Boxwood, faience, rock crystal, silk. Name it; the model renders surfaces by their names.

notes.head: Size
notes.body: Say how big it is: this netsuke fits in a palm. Without a size the model picks one.

notes.head: What must not change
notes.body: List it first in the prompt: the face, the carving, the colour of the wood.

images.label: Object 2
images.caption: Netsuke, Japan, 18th century. Carved wood, palm-sized. Met 10.211.2273. CC0.

chapters.title: Six rules for a plate
chapters.dek: Follow these for every picture in the set.

notes.head: Say what stays
notes.body: Begin with what must not change: the object's exact shape, colour and material.

notes.head: One ground for the whole book
notes.body: Pure seamless black. Paste the same words into every prompt.

notes.head: One light
notes.body: A large soft key from above left, a thin rim, no fill. Shadows stay deep and clean.

notes.head: Fix the seed
notes.body: Use one seed for the set, so a change in the picture comes from a change in the words.

notes.head: Give it a size
notes.body: Toy scale, palm-sized, 4 cm across. Scale words change the lens the model imagines.

notes.head: Set the type yourself
notes.body: Models garble small lettering. Ask for blank panels and set every title and caption in layout, as this book does.

images.label: Object 3
images.caption: Watch, ca. 1630–40. Rock crystal case, enamelled dial. Met 17.190.1525. CC0.

chapters.title: One object per plate
chapters.dek: A plate is made from its own object alone.

notes.head: What run 1 did
notes.body: Each object plate also took the cover as image 2, as a lighting reference. For object 3 the model copied the cover hippo into the plate instead of the watch.

notes.head: The fix
notes.body: Run 2 feeds each plate only its own object. The shared House look text carries the light, ground and camera.

notes.head: What held
notes.body: With one seed and one House look, the three plates still share a black ground and a soft key from above left.

notes.head: Keep the reject
notes.body: The run 1 plate is kept as a record of the failure. It is not used anywhere else in this book.

images.label: Run 1  Rejected
images.caption: Plate 03 with the cover as image 2: the watch is gone, the hippo came back. AI-generated.

images.label: Run 2  Seed 20261103
images.caption: Plate 03 from the watch alone. AI-generated.

chapters.title: A plate on black
chapters.dek: One object, one light, nothing else in the frame.

notes.head: Why black
notes.body: It drops the room. Every plate in a set can sit on the same ground, so they read as one series.

notes.head: Leave space
notes.body: Ask for the object small in the frame. Cropping in later is easy; the model cannot add black it never drew.

notes.head: Check the edges
notes.body: Look for halos and grey fog where the ground should be flat. Reject, do not retouch.

notes.head: Keep the record
notes.body: ComfyUI writes the whole graph into each PNG. Drop one back onto the canvas to get every setting back.

images.label: Plate 02  Seed 20261103
images.caption: plate-book.json, run 2: the netsuke. Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, Lightning, 4 steps, CFG 1. AI-generated.

chapters.title: Three objects, one ground
chapters.dek: One seed and one House look across the set.

notes.head: Same words
notes.body: Every plate prompt is the plate instruction, then the House look, then the Book prompt. Only the first part changes.

notes.head: One seed
notes.body: All five plates use seed 20261103, so a change in a plate comes from its words or its input.

notes.head: What held
notes.body: Black ground, a soft key from above left and a deep shadow under each object carry through all three plates.

notes.head: What varied
notes.body: Size: each plate keeps the shape of its input photo, scaled to the nearest preset, so the hippo is portrait, the netsuke landscape and the watch square.

chapters.title: The group plate
chapters.dek: The three plates, set out together.

notes.head: Plates in, not photos
notes.body: The group plate takes plates 01, 02 and 03 as images 1, 2 and 3, so the objects arrive already lit and cut out.

notes.head: What held
notes.body: All three objects are present and recognisable: glaze pattern, carving and the enamelled dial.

notes.head: What drifted
notes.body: The model added a dark tray with a curved rim. The prompt asked for objects like specimens on a museum tray, and it took the words literally.

notes.head: Not retouched
notes.body: Faint white specks sit in the lower third of the black ground. They are in the raw output and were left as they are.

images.label: Plate 04  Seed 20261103
images.caption: plate-book.json, run 2: group plate made from plates 01–03. Raw output, not retouched. AI-generated.

chapters.title: Choosing the cover
chapters.dek: One plate, mapped by brightness to a short scale of tones.

notes.head: Brightness only
notes.body: The plate is turned to grey, then each grey is given a colour from the scale. Hue in the original is ignored.

notes.head: Seven tones
notes.body: Near-black, ink blue, oxblood, rust, amber, sand, paper. The scale is printed beside the cover so the mapping can be read.

notes.head: Dark plates work best
notes.body: A specimen on black puts most of the picture in the lowest tones, so the object glows in the warm ones.

notes.head: Change the scale
notes.body: Edit tone_scale in the spec. Any number of tones, darkest first.

images.label: Before
images.caption: Plate 00 from plate-book.json, as generated. AI-generated.

images.label: After
images.caption: The same picture mapped to the cover scale by make_book.py.

chapters.title: From a folder to a book
chapters.dek: Run the workflow, then the layout script.

notes.head: Collect
notes.body: Put up to three object photos in ComfyUI/input as collection_01.png to collection_03.png.

notes.head: Write the prompt
notes.body: One paragraph on what the book is about. It goes into the Book prompt box and onto page 2.

notes.head: Run plate-book.json
notes.body: One run makes a cover plate, one plate per object and a group plate, all on black.

notes.head: Pick
notes.body: Keep the plates that pass the checks in chapter 05. Run again with a new seed, or change the words, for the rest.

notes.head: Caption
notes.body: Write a label and a line for each image in book.json, with its seed and source.

notes.head: Build
notes.body: python scripts/make_book.py --spec book.json --images folder --out out. A PDF and spreads come out.
